1. (Currently Amended) A method, comprising: inputting database constructs generated by a database optimizer as an input to a trained machine-learning algorithm that has been trained on historical database performance data; obtaining a database operation predictor from the machine-learning algorithm as an output, wherein the database operation predictor comprises a predicted performance metric not previously stored in database statistics; modifying at least one of the database constructs based on the database operation predictor producing a modified database construct that differs from query execution plans previously generated by the database optimizer; and processing a database operation with the database constructs and the modified database construct.

2. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein inputting further includes inputting the database constructs as query execution plans for a query, and wherein the trained machine-learning algorithm receives as input a combination of multiple query execution plans including non-least-cost alternatives.

3. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 2, wherein inputting further includes identifying at least one database construct as a least cost query execution plan identified from the query execution plans by the database optimizer, and wherein the machine-learning algorithm is trained to predict performance outcomes that contradict the least cost designation.

4. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 3, wherein identifying further includes identifying individual pieces of the least cost query execution plan as: a total number of spools used, cardinality for tables with any intermediate results used, a total number of merge joins, a total number of hash joins, nested loop joins, references for the spools, and costs per database resource assigned by the database optimizer, and wherein the machine-learning algorithm generates predictions based on interactions between these individual pieces rather than individual piece analysis alone.

5. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated Central Process Unit (CPU) execution time for one or more Access Module Processors to execute when processing the database operation, wherein the estimated CPU execution time is generated through machine-learning pattern recognition across multiple historical query executions.

6. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein obtaining further includes acquiring the database operation predictor as an estimated number of Input/Output (I/O) operations performed by one or more Access Module Processors during execution when processing the database operation, wherein the estimated number of I/O operations is generated through machine-learning pattern recognition across multiple historical query executions.

7. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a scheduled execution time for the database operation as the modified database construct based on the database operation predictor indicating that the scheduled execution time will result in resource contention.

8. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a scheduled execution time for execution of a query as the modified database construct based on the database operation predictor indicating that the scheduled execution time will result in resource contention.

9. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein modifying further includes changing a workgroup assigned to the database operation as the modified database construct based on the database operation predictor indicating that the current workgroup assignment will result in Service Level Agreement violations.

10. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 1 further comprising, storing the database operation predictor in database statistics associated with the database operation and the database constructs, wherein the database operation predictor is stored in association with metadata indicating the specific machine-learning model version and training dataset used to generate the predictor.

11. (Original) The method of claim 10 further comprising, rendering an interface from the database statistics depicting relationships between the database operation, the database operation predictor, the database constructs, and the modified database construct with respect to other instances of the database operation, other database operation predictors, other database constructs, and other modified database constructs.

12. (Currently Amended) A method comprising: training a machine-learning algorithm with database constructs produced by a database optimizer using historical performance data that includes actual execution times that deviate from optimizer cost estimates; receiving query execution plans for a query from the database optimizer with a least cost query execution plan identified by the database optimizer for the query; providing the query execution plans as input to the machine-learning algorithm; obtaining as an output a predicted execution time for the query based on the least cost query execution plan, wherein the predicted execution time is generated through machine-learning pattern recognition rather than cost-based estimation; and modifying one of: the least cost query execution plan for the query, a scheduled execution time for the query, and resources that are used to execute the query based on the predicted execution time differing from the optimizer's cost estimate.

13. (Original) The method of claim 12 further comprising, notifying a database administrator when based on the predicted execution time a Service Level Goal (SLG) or Service Level Agreement (SLA) associated with the query will be unable to be satisfied using the least cost query execution plan or using a modified version of the least cost query execution plan that was modified based on the predicted execution time.

14. (Original) The method of claim 12 further comprising: providing an interface rendered through a database tool that models the database constructs, the query execution plans, an actual query execution time for the query, and the predicted execution time for the query against other queries having other database constructs, other query execution plans, other actual query execution times for the other queries, and other predicted execution times provided by the machine-learning algorithm for the other queries.

15. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12, wherein providing further includes providing the database tool within a workload scheduler and management component of a database system.

16. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12, wherein training further includes training the machine-learning algorithm as a linear regression-based machine-learning algorithm that incorporates non-linear feature interactions derived from the database constructs.

17. (Original) The method of claim 12, wherein modifying further includes selecting a different one of the query execution plans to execute the query instead of the least cost query execution plan based on the predicted execution time and a historical actual execution time known for the different query execution plan.

18. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 12, wherein modifying further includes changing an execution resource of the least cost query execution plan based on the predicted query execution time and a current performance associated with the execution resource, wherein the execution resource change is determined by the machine-learning algorithm to optimize for metrics other than cost.

19. (Currently Amended) A system, comprising: a database management system; at least one hardware processor; a non-transitory computer-readable storage medium having executable instructions representing a trained machine-learning algorithm that has been trained on historical database performance data including actual execution times that deviate from optimizer cost estimates; the machine learning algorithm configured to execute on the at least one hardware processor from the non-transitory computer-readable storage medium and to perform processing to: i) receive as input database constructs produced by a database optimizer for a database operation of the database management system; and ii) provide as output a predicted value relevant to one of: one or more of the database constructs and the database operation, wherein the predicted value is generated through machine-learning pattern recognition rather than cost-based estimation; wherein the database management system is configured to process the predicted value to determine whether to modify one of: the one or more database constructs and the database operation before processing the database operation within the database management system.

20. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 19, wherein the predicted value is an estimated query execution time for a query that differs from the optimizer's cost estimate, and the database operation is execution of a query execution plan for the query within the database management system.
